title: U.S. House · California's 47th District
area: Coastal and central Orange County, including Irvine and surrounding communities. Redrawn under Proposition 50 (approved November 2025).

context.text: Incumbent Dave Min (D) and Republican Jenny Rae Le Roux advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary; Min received 45.4% of the vote and Le Roux 25.0%, ahead of seven other candidates.

candidates.name: Dave Min
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 45.4% of the vote.

summary.text: Dave Min is the Democratic incumbent in the 47th District, first elected to the U.S. House in 2024. He began his career as an SEC enforcement attorney, later became a UC Irvine law professor, and served in the California State Senate from 2020 to 2024. His campaign materials emphasize abortion access, gun violence prevention, climate action and protections for domestic-violence survivors.

background.text: Born in Providence, Rhode Island, and raised in Palo Alto, California, the child of Korean immigrants; his official bio describes him as a product of California public schools.
Earned a B.S. in economics from the Wharton School and a B.A. in philosophy from the University of Pennsylvania in 1999, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 2002.

Began his career as an enforcement attorney at the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, and later worked as a policy advisor to Sen. Chuck Schumer and as an economic policy director at the Center for American Progress.
Became a law professor at UC Irvine in 2012, teaching and researching business law and focusing on banking and housing policy; his official bio says he testified six times before Congress.
Ran for Congress in 2018 in the 45th District, finishing third in the top-two primary behind Rep. Mimi Walters and Katie Porter.

Served in the California State Senate from December 2020 to 2024 after narrowly defeating Republican incumbent John Moorlach in 2020; he chaired the Natural Resources and Water Committee and authored the state's 30x30 land and coastal conservation law.

In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he says he passed 28 bills into law in the State Senate, including eight protecting domestic-violence survivors; his official bio says he authored more than 30 laws.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2024, succeeding Katie Porter; he serves on the Natural Resources Committee and the Oversight and Government Reform Committee.
According to his official bio, he lives in Irvine with his wife, Jane, and their three children.

priorities.text: Reproductive freedom, citing his authorship of a California constitutional amendment on abortion and contraception access.
Gun violence prevention, citing legislation he passed prohibiting gun shows on state property.
Climate action, citing legislation he authored to end offshore oil drilling.

positions.summary: Says he authored a California ballot proposition adding abortion and contraception access to the state constitution and has a 100% rating from Planned Parenthood.
Says he passed state legislation prohibiting gun shows on state property and has an 'F' rating from the NRA.
Says he authored legislation to end offshore oil drilling and reduce reliance on fossil fuels, and has a 100% rating from the Sierra Club.

record.text: Serves on the Joint Economic Committee, the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, and the Committee on Natural Resources for the 2025-2026 term.
As a California state senator, sponsored roughly 28 bills that were enacted, including eight related to protections for domestic-violence survivors, according to his campaign.

candidates.name: Jenny Rae Le Roux
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with 25.0% of the vote.

summary.text: Jenny Rae Le Roux is the Republican candidate in the 47th District. She is a business owner and management executive who ran for California governor as a Republican in the 2021 recall election and the 2022 regular election. She currently serves as director of CAL DOGE, an initiative tied to Republican statewide candidates, and says her work there led her to run for Congress.

background.text: Earned a B.A. in economics from the University of Virginia in 2002 and an M.B.A. from Columbia Business School in 2018.
Career experience includes owning a business and working as managing director of Management Consulted, as well as working as an author and strategic advisor.
She told Fox News that she had a farm, a family and a business, and that the COVID-19 pandemic led her to become politically active.
Ran for governor of California as a Republican in the 2021 recall election and again in the 2022 election, finishing fourth in the June 2022 primary with 3.5% of the vote.
Serves as director of CAL DOGE, an initiative launched by Republican gubernatorial candidate Steve Hilton and state controller candidate Herb Morgan.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary in the 47th District with 25.0% of the vote, second to Rep. Dave Min.
Endorsed in this race by the Republican Party of California.

priorities.text: Public safety, citing rising crime rates and reduced sentencing in California as reasons to increase police staffing.

positions.summary: In her 2022 gubernatorial campaign, said she would work to retain and hire new police officers, support pay increases for officers, and stop prison closures.

candidates.researchNotes: Her documented policy statements are from her 2022 campaign for governor, the most detailed public record found; no 2026 congressional-campaign website content was located.
